runs.text: 1. Moderate and improving leverage on a company-defined measure (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1 leverage chart table and Calculations). Carvana's total debt including finance leases was USD 5,261 million at Q3 2026 against LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,752 million, a ratio of 1.91x, down from 2.29x at FY2025; net of USD 3,049 million of unrestricted cash the ratio is 0.80x. The mechanism is EBITDA growth on a flat debt stock, so the improvement reflects earnings rather than repayment. Of the debt, USD 1,125 million is asset-based financing; corporate funded debt of USD 4,036 million is 1.47x. Including trade floor plan payables of USD 300 million the ratio is 2.02x. 2. Earnings quality is the central financial weakness (Analyst Interpretation; basis: CP-1 Credit analysis on cash flow quality and CP-1A Calculations). Loan sale gains of USD 1,084 million were 48.4% of nine-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,241 million, while operating cash flow was USD 900 million, 40.2% of that EBITDA, and free cash flow after purchases of property and equipment was USD 734 million. The mechanism is that gains are recognised when loans are sold and the cash arrives through sale proceeds, with growth absorbing working capital. A pull-back by loan buyers would cut gain on sale and cash conversion at the same time. 3. Cash interest cover is adequate but did not improve with leverage (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1 interest cover chart table). Cover was 5.88x at Q3 2026, the lowest of four dates, because cash interest paid rose as former payment-in-kind coupons turned to cash, even though interest expense, net fell. The August 2026 refinancing lowers the stated coupon, but the interest hedge ends on July 31, 2028 while the term loan runs to 2033. 4. Liquidity is strong on cash and conditional on collateral (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1 liquidity chart table and liquidity by facility). Carvana held USD 3,049 million of cash and USD 2,071 million of borrowing-base availability against USD 5,600 million of revolving commitments, of which USD 71 million was drawn; commitments of USD 3,900 million mature within twelve months after the October 2026 extension. The mechanism is renewal risk on lines that fund inventory and receivables; a market shock that cuts renewals and loan-sale capacity together would hit both sources. 5. Control and related-party dependence cannot be tested (Documentary Fact for the facts, Insufficient Information for capacity; basis: CP-1A ownership, governance and operating model rows). The Garcia Parties hold about 83% of the voting power, and DriveTime, which they own, administers service contracts and warranties; its commissions are 21.2% of other sales and revenues and 8.4% of gross profit for the nine months. Ally, which lends on the floor plan, bought about 41.0% of the principal of loans sold. The documented record since 2023 is supportive (equity purchase, equity-funded note redemption, no dividends), but the agreements that would limit extraction or priming are not in the pack. 6. Claims outside the debt figure add to fixed obligations (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1 Claims outside the debt figure). The tax receivable agreement liability is USD 2,230 million, operating lease liabilities USD 469 million, and trade floor plan payables USD 300 million, equal to the size of that line. None is in the leverage ratio. 7. The term loan refinancing was debt neutral (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1 Latest quarter and CP-1A Transaction summary). A USD 1,660 million term loan priced at Term SOFR plus 2.25% replaced USD 1,660 million of 9% secured notes, moving the maturity to 2033 and ranking pari passu with the 2031 secured notes. No financial maintenance covenant applies to the term loan, so headroom is not measurable.

runs.text: Strengths. Carvana has scale and momentum: retail units rose 39.4% in Q3 2026, and Adjusted EBITDA reached USD 800 million in the quarter (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1A operating model row on volume and CP-1 financial table). Management describes the platform as the leading one in its market, which is Management Language and is not adopted. Carvana has liquidity depth, with USD 3,049 million of cash and a broad set of revolving and loan-sale lines (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1 liquidity tables and CP-1A loan sale model row). Its leverage has fallen at each of four balance sheet dates and its term-out of the 2030 secured notes removed the largest near-dated bullet shown in the printed schedule (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1 leverage and maturities chart tables). The documented conduct of the controlling holders since 2023 is supportive: equity support, equity-funded redemption and no dividends (Analyst Interpretation; basis: CP-1A governance and sponsor behaviour table).

Weaknesses. Carvana's earnings depend on gain on sale: loan sale gains are 48.4% of nine-month Adjusted EBITDA, and other revenue carries no cost of sales, so margin follows funding markets (Analyst Interpretation; basis: CP-1 Credit analysis and CP-1A operating model rows). Unit economics are thinner: total gross profit per unit fell to USD 6,997 in Q3 2026 from USD 7,362, and Adjusted EBITDA margin was 10.0% on an LTM basis against 11.0% in FY2025 (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1A unit economics row and CP-1 financial table). Management attributes the decline to giving back lower loan rates, which is Management Language. Carvana's funding is short-dated and collateral-limited, with counterparty concentration in Ally and DriveTime (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1 liquidity by facility and CP-1A Calculations). Control by one group, related-party dealings and a tax receivable liability to related parties are not constrained by any document in the pack (Insufficient Information on capacity; basis: CP-1A ownership and governance rows). Covenant levels, guarantor schedules and a post-refinancing maturity schedule are missing, so protection and refinancing risk cannot be measured (Insufficient Information; basis: CP-0 and CP-1 gaps).

runs.text: The only new debt issue in the latest quarter is the term loan. On August 14, 2026, Carvana Co. entered into a credit agreement for a senior secured term loan B, fully drawn at closing at an issue price of 99.75% of principal [10-Q Q3 2026, page:26, "which was fully drawn at closing at an issue price of 99.75%"]. The agreement is listed with the lenders and Barclays Bank PLC as administrative agent [10-Q Q3 2026, page:88, "Barclays Bank PLC, as Administrative Agent and Syndication Agent"]. Use of proceeds: together with cash on hand, the proceeds redeemed in full the 2030 Senior Secured Notes [10-Q Q3 2026, page:25, "to redeem in full its 2030 Senior Secured Notes"]. Status: closed and drawn at the balance sheet date; the redemption is complete and treated as an extinguishment with a loss recognised in the quarter. Debt raised and retired are equal in principal (the amounts are in the CP-1 handoff); the premium paid on redemption came from cash, so the liquidity effect is a cash outflow equal to that premium with no change in debt. The CP-1 handoff logs a conflict on the accrued interest component of the redemption payment (1 in Note 9 against 4 in the management discussion); it is carried here as logged and not reconciled.

Terms that matter to creditors: the term loan is floating (Term SOFR plus a margin), amortizes 1.00% a year from March 2027, matures in 2033, ranks pari passu with the 2031 secured notes on the same first-priority collateral, and has no financial maintenance covenant [10-Q Q3 2026, page:27, "ranking pari passu with the Company's outstanding Senior Secured Notes"]. An interest rate swap hedges only to July 31, 2028, so rate exposure returns for the remaining life [10-Q Q3 2026, page:52, "terminates on July 31, 2028"]. Prepayments through February 14, 2027 in connection with certain repricing transactions carry a 1.00% premium. The effect on the secured group is that the new lenders share the collateral equally with the remaining noteholders; the pro rata share of each depends on the principal amounts in the CP-1 handoff, and no intercreditor agreement is supplied. The preferred unit mechanism mirrors the debt: for each note retired one preferred unit of Carvana Group is retired, and one is issued for the term loan [10-Q Q3 2026, page:33, "issued 1.66 million of Class A Non-Convertible Preferred Units in conjunction with the incurrence of the Term Loan B"].

Earlier new financings in the evidence window: a fleet financing agreement with Citizens Bank in October 2025, a trade floor plan line with Stellantis Financial Services tied to franchise dealership purchases, and a seventh finance receivable facility in May 2026. Sale-capacity amendments with Ally (to a larger commitment through July 2027) and a loan purchase agreement upsize are receivable sales, not debt. No financial sponsor is involved, and no equity was raised through the at-the-market program in 2026; it had no activity in the first nine months [10-Q Q3 2026, page:32, "There was no activity pursuant to the ATM Program during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026."]. Subsequent to the quarter, the third finance receivable lender's maturity was extended to October 15, 2027; this is a subsequent event and is not folded into the September 30 facts.

fields.value: On the company's own measure, leverage is moderate and falling. Total debt including finance leases is 5,261 at September 30, 2026 against LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 2,752, a ratio of 1.91x, and net of unrestricted cash of 3,049 the ratio is 0.80x. The ratio has fallen at each of the four balance sheet dates read (FY2025 2.29x, Q1 2026 2.14x, Q2 2026 2.03x, Q3 2026 1.91x), driven by LTM EBITDA growth from 2,237 to 2,752 on debt that moved little. The headline understates three features. First, 1,125 of the debt is secured asset-based financing (floor plan, financing of retained securitization interests, sale-leaseback real estate financing and fleet financing), which is not corporate funded debt; the senior notes, term loan and unsecured notes total 4,036 (1.47x). Second, Adjusted EBITDA is a company-defined measure that includes loan sale gains (1,084 in nine months 2026, 48.4% of the nine-month Adjusted EBITDA of 2,241) and adds back share-based compensation, while operating cash flow for those nine months was 900. Third, claims outside the debt figure add to fixed obligations: the tax receivable agreement liability (2,230), operating leases (469), and trade floor plan payables (300) that sit in accounts payable.

The August 2026 refinancing (a 1,660 term loan at Term SOFR plus 2.25%, replacing 1,660 of 9% notes) lowers the stated coupon, but the interest rate swap hedges only to July 31, 2028 and the term loan matures in 2033.

Most commitments mature within twelve months of the balance sheet date. No financial maintenance covenant applies to the term loan, and compliance with all debt covenants is stated; covenant levels and headroom for the other facilities are Not supplied. The view is a base for the credit snapshot, not a credit conclusion; the four limits above and the gaps in `## Gaps` apply to every use of it.

fields.value: - Leverage. Evidence: total debt including finance leases over LTM Adjusted EBITDA fell from 2.29x to 1.91x across four dates, while net debt fell from 2,806 to 2,212 as cash rose. Mechanism: EBITDA growth outpaced a flat debt stock, and the refinancing was debt neutral (1,660 in, 1,660 out) with a premium of 50 paid from cash. Implication: leverage is moderate on the company measure; of the debt, 1,125 is asset-based, so the measure mixes funding of inventory, receivables and property with corporate debt. Excluding asset-based debt, corporate funded debt is 4,036 (1.47x). Including trade floor plan payables (300) the ratio is 2.02x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Coverage. Evidence: cash interest rose to 443 in nine months from 311 while interest expense, net fell to 298 from 407. Mechanism: the secured notes moved from payment-in-kind to cash coupons during 2025, so reported expense fell while cash paid rose; the refinancing then reduced the stated coupon on 1,660. Implication: cash cover of 5.88x is the right measure; it is the lowest of the four dates, so cover did not improve with leverage. Comparisons across the refinancing are not like for like.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash flow quality. Evidence: nine months operating cash flow 900 against Adjusted EBITDA 2,241; vehicle inventory used 1,025 and accounts payable and accrued liabilities provided 475. Mechanism: growth consumes working capital, and Adjusted EBITDA includes non-cash gain on loan sales (1,084) whose cash arrives through receivable sales in operating cash flow. Implication: free cash flow after purchases of property and equipment was 734 in nine months 2026 (900 less 166), well below EBITDA; the credit depends on continued access to receivable sale and financing markets.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity. Evidence: cash 3,049 and availability 2,071; maturities cluster within twelve months. Mechanism: revolvers are borrowing-base limited and renewed routinely, and the receivable sale arrangements are committed with terms into 2027 and early 2028. Implication: day-to-day liquidity is adequate; a market disruption that cuts renewals or sale capacity would hit the 5,600 revolving lines and the sale capacity together.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Carvana Co. is a holding company whose operating business sits in Carvana Group, LLC, a vertically integrated online retailer of used vehicles: it buys cars from consumers and wholesalers, reconditions them in owned sites, sells and delivers them nationally, finances customers, and sells the loans it originates. Management calls itself the leading platform in its market, which is Management Language; the filings document the model but not the ranking. The creditor-relevant mechanics are these. Revenue is anchored on retail units, and every other stream (wholesale, loan sale gains, complementary products) is created by a retail sale, so volume, used-vehicle pricing and consumer credit availability move together. Profit depends heavily on selling loans into committed and market channels at a gain; that links earnings to the appetite of a few buyers and to benchmark rates, and management says it chose to give back margin to customers through lower loan rates. Funding is layered: corporate secured and unsecured debt at the holding company, plus asset-backed lines at operating and special purpose subsidiaries, as set out in the CP-1 handoff.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership and governance matter to creditors more than usual. The Garcia Parties control most of the voting power through ten-vote Class B shares, the company is a controlled company, and DriveTime, owned by the same parties, supplies services on which revenue depends. The documented conduct since 2023 is mostly supportive (an equity purchase to fund a note tender, equity issuance to redeem secured notes, no dividends), but the agreements that limit what the controlling group could do are not in the pack, so capacity to act against creditors cannot be assessed. The only transaction in the latest quarter is the August 2026 refinancing, which left the debt amount unchanged and moved cost, maturity and rate profile. Subsequent to the quarter, one revolving facility was extended.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The only new debt issue in the latest quarter is the term loan. On August 14, 2026, Carvana Co. entered into a credit agreement for a senior secured term loan B, fully drawn at closing at an issue price of 99.75% of principal [10-Q Q3 2026, page:26, "which was fully drawn at closing at an issue price of 99.75%"]. The agreement is listed with the lenders and Barclays Bank PLC as administrative agent [10-Q Q3 2026, page:88, "Barclays Bank PLC, as Administrative Agent and Syndication Agent"]. Use of proceeds: together with cash on hand, the proceeds redeemed in full the 2030 Senior Secured Notes [10-Q Q3 2026, page:25, "to redeem in full its 2030 Senior Secured Notes"]. Status: closed and drawn at the balance sheet date; the redemption is complete and treated as an extinguishment with a loss recognised in the quarter. Debt raised and retired are equal in principal (the amounts are in the CP-1 handoff); the premium paid on redemption came from cash, so the liquidity effect is a cash outflow equal to that premium with no change in debt. The CP-1 handoff logs a conflict on the accrued interest component of the redemption payment (1 in Note 9 against 4 in the management discussion); it is carried here as logged and not reconciled.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Terms that matter to creditors: the term loan is floating (Term SOFR plus a margin), amortizes 1.00% a year from March 2027, matures in 2033, ranks pari passu with the 2031 secured notes on the same first-priority collateral, and has no financial maintenance covenant [10-Q Q3 2026, page:27, "ranking pari passu with the Company's outstanding Senior Secured Notes"]. An interest rate swap hedges only to July 31, 2028, so rate exposure returns for the remaining life [10-Q Q3 2026, page:52, "terminates on July 31, 2028"]. Prepayments through February 14, 2027 in connection with certain repricing transactions carry a 1.00% premium. The effect on the secured group is that the new lenders share the collateral equally with the remaining noteholders; the pro rata share of each depends on the principal amounts in the CP-1 handoff, and no intercreditor agreement is supplied. The preferred unit mechanism mirrors the debt: for each note retired one preferred unit of Carvana Group is retired, and one is issued for the term loan [10-Q Q3 2026, page:33, "issued 1.66 million of Class A Non-Convertible Preferred Units in conjunction with the incurrence of the Term Loan B"].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earlier new financings in the evidence window: a fleet financing agreement with Citizens Bank in October 2025, a trade floor plan line with Stellantis Financial Services tied to franchise dealership purchases, and a seventh finance receivable facility in May 2026. Sale-capacity amendments with Ally (to a larger commitment through July 2027) and a loan purchase agreement upsize are receivable sales, not debt. No financial sponsor is involved, and no equity was raised through the at-the-market program in 2026; it had no activity in the first nine months [10-Q Q3 2026, page:32, "There was no activity pursuant to the ATM Program during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026."]. Subsequent to the quarter, the third finance receivable lender's maturity was extended to October 15, 2027; this is a subsequent event and is not folded into the September 30 facts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Carvana has a sound but market-dependent fundamental credit profile: its debt is moderate against earnings, but those earnings depend on consumers, loan buyers and funding lines that can tighten together. The strongest support is financial. Total debt including finance leases of USD 5,261 million is 1.91x LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,752 million, and unrestricted cash of USD 3,049 million brings net leverage to 0.80x. The weakest point is quality and structure. Adjusted EBITDA includes loan sale gains equal to 48.4% of nine-month Adjusted EBITDA, operating cash flow trails EBITDA, and the control and related-party dealings of the Garcia Parties cannot be tested because the governing documents are not supplied. Continued access to loan sales and renewal of revolvers decide the outcome.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The confidence is below High because no executed financing document is available, the post-refinancing maturity schedule is not printed, and ratings are Not supplied (see `## Gaps`).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. Moderate and improving leverage on a company-defined measure (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1 leverage chart table and Calculations). Carvana's total debt including finance leases was USD 5,261 million at Q3 2026 against LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,752 million, a ratio of 1.91x, down from 2.29x at FY2025; net of USD 3,049 million of unrestricted cash the ratio is 0.80x. The mechanism is EBITDA growth on a flat debt stock, so the improvement reflects earnings rather than repayment. Of the debt, USD 1,125 million is asset-based financing; corporate funded debt of USD 4,036 million is 1.47x. Including trade floor plan payables of USD 300 million the ratio is 2.02x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Earnings quality is the central financial weakness (Analyst Interpretation; basis: CP-1 Credit analysis on cash flow quality and CP-1A Calculations). Loan sale gains of USD 1,084 million were 48.4% of nine-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,241 million, while operating cash flow was USD 900 million, 40.2% of that EBITDA, and free cash flow after purchases of property and equipment was USD 734 million. The mechanism is that gains are recognised when loans are sold and the cash arrives through sale proceeds, with growth absorbing working capital. A pull-back by loan buyers would cut gain on sale and cash conversion at the same time.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Cash interest cover is adequate but did not improve with leverage (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1 interest cover chart table). Cover was 5.88x at Q3 2026, the lowest of four dates, because cash interest paid rose as former payment-in-kind coupons turned to cash, even though interest expense, net fell. The August 2026 refinancing lowers the stated coupon, but the interest hedge ends on July 31, 2028 while the term loan runs to 2033.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. Liquidity is strong on cash and conditional on collateral (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1 liquidity chart table and liquidity by facility). Carvana held USD 3,049 million of cash and USD 2,071 million of borrowing-base availability against USD 5,600 million of revolving commitments, of which USD 71 million was drawn; commitments of USD 3,900 million mature within twelve months after the October 2026 extension. The mechanism is renewal risk on lines that fund inventory and receivables; a market shock that cuts renewals and loan-sale capacity together would hit both sources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 5. Control and related-party dependence cannot be tested (Documentary Fact for the facts, Insufficient Information for capacity; basis: CP-1A ownership, governance and operating model rows). The Garcia Parties hold about 83% of the voting power, and DriveTime, which they own, administers service contracts and warranties; its commissions are 21.2% of other sales and revenues and 8.4% of gross profit for the nine months. Ally, which lends on the floor plan, bought about 41.0% of the principal of loans sold. The documented record since 2023 is supportive (equity purchase, equity-funded note redemption, no dividends), but the agreements that would limit extraction or priming are not in the pack.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 6. Claims outside the debt figure add to fixed obligations (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1 Claims outside the debt figure). The tax receivable agreement liability is USD 2,230 million, operating lease liabilities USD 469 million, and trade floor plan payables USD 300 million, equal to the size of that line. None is in the leverage ratio.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 7. The term loan refinancing was debt neutral (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1 Latest quarter and CP-1A Transaction summary). A USD 1,660 million term loan priced at Term SOFR plus 2.25% replaced USD 1,660 million of 9% secured notes, moving the maturity to 2033 and ranking pari passu with the 2031 secured notes. No financial maintenance covenant applies to the term loan, so headroom is not measurable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Carvana has scale and momentum: retail units rose 39.4% in Q3 2026, and Adjusted EBITDA reached USD 800 million in the quarter (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1A operating model row on volume and CP-1 financial table). Management describes the platform as the leading one in its market, which is Management Language and is not adopted. Carvana has liquidity depth, with USD 3,049 million of cash and a broad set of revolving and loan-sale lines (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1 liquidity tables and CP-1A loan sale model row). Its leverage has fallen at each of four balance sheet dates and its term-out of the 2030 secured notes removed the largest near-dated bullet shown in the printed schedule (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1 leverage and maturities chart tables). The documented conduct of the controlling holders since 2023 is supportive: equity support, equity-funded redemption and no dividends (Analyst Interpretation; basis: CP-1A governance and sponsor behaviour table).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Carvana's earnings depend on gain on sale: loan sale gains are 48.4% of nine-month Adjusted EBITDA, and other revenue carries no cost of sales, so margin follows funding markets (Analyst Interpretation; basis: CP-1 Credit analysis and CP-1A operating model rows). Unit economics are thinner: total gross profit per unit fell to USD 6,997 in Q3 2026 from USD 7,362, and Adjusted EBITDA margin was 10.0% on an LTM basis against 11.0% in FY2025 (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1A unit economics row and CP-1 financial table). Management attributes the decline to giving back lower loan rates, which is Management Language. Carvana's funding is short-dated and collateral-limited, with counterparty concentration in Ally and DriveTime (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1 liquidity by facility and CP-1A Calculations). Control by one group, related-party dealings and a tax receivable liability to related parties are not constrained by any document in the pack (Insufficient Information on capacity; basis: CP-1A ownership and governance rows). Covenant levels, guarantor schedules and a post-refinancing maturity schedule are missing, so protection and refinancing risk cannot be measured (Insufficient Information; basis: CP-0 and CP-1 gaps).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The analysis of Carvana is traceable enough for a restricted committee use but not for a clean one. The strongest support is mechanical: every cited quote was found verbatim on its cited page, the derived figures recomputed exactly, and the CP-1, CP-1A and CP-2 figures agree with one another. The weakest point is evidential: the maturity chart still shows the schedule printed before the August 2026 refinancing, including the 2030 Senior Secured Notes that were redeemed, and legal structure, guarantor perimeter, debt baskets and control limits are described only as the issuer describes them because no executed document is in the pack. Two issues are Material and five are Minor, with none Critical. Supplying the financing documents and rebuilding the maturity chart would lift the restriction.
